_about: Landmark classification rules. Hand-authored; resolved against mapgrouppos.xml.
TRACEABILITY. Every rule below is applied to the live building list at build time and
the result is recorded in docs/data/provenance.json: which class names each rule
matched, how many instances, and the sha256 of the source file it matched against.
A rule that matches NOTHING fails the build.
That check exists because it already failed silently once: a `Hunting|Chalet|Cabin`
rule was added and matched zero buildings, shipping an empty layer that looked
deliberate. Counts alone would not have caught it -- the rule has to be forced to
SCOPE LIMIT, and it is a real one: mapgrouppos.xml lists only buildings the Central
Economy puts loot in. Structures that hold no loot -- most tall radio masts, water
towers, chimneys, the things you actually navigate by at distance -- are NOT in any
published Bohemia data. The full terrain object list lives in the PBOs. So this file
can never be a complete landmark set, only a complete LOOT-BEARING landmark set.
Order matters: first match wins, so specific rules precede general ones.
`optional: true` allows zero matches for rules kept for other terrains.

_notes.well: Wells and water stations matter to the run planner specifically: a route costs water, and these are where you get it back.
_notes.radiotower: Land_Tower_TC1 also matches `watchtower`. First match wins, so it lands under radiotower -- deliberate, they are the same tall structure you navigate by.
_notes.missing: No entry can exist here for a structure absent from mapgrouppos.xml. See the scope limit above.
_notes.ordering: watchtower precedes military deliberately: ^Land_Mil_ would otherwise consume Land_Mil_GuardTower and Land_Mil_Fortified_Nest_Watchtower, and the build's zero-match check caught exactly that.
